evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry for 和 lists 咊 and 龢 among variant forms and reproduces the Shuowen account: “相應也。从口，禾聲” (responding; from 口, with 禾 as phonetic), with 戶戈切. This supports the Han lexicographic analysis, not the graph’s earliest origin.
evidence.title: [A00556] 和 - Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Varients》2024

evidence.text: The entry classifies 禾 and 和 in the same phonetic series. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction, 禾 is *ɡoːl, while 和 has *ɡoːl and *ɡoːls. The page gives modern Mandarin 禾 hé and historical Middle Chinese hwa. This supports 禾’s sound role; no claim that the grain meaning contributes to 和 follows from it.
evidence.title: 和 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The 禾 entry gives modern Mandarin hé, Middle Chinese hwa, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[ɢ]ˤoj. The 和 entry gives hé, hwa, and *[ɢ]ˤoj for the harmonious reading, and a distinct hè, hwaH, *[ɢ]ˤoj-s reading for musical response/tuning. These reconstructions support sound correspondence within the cited system; they do not establish a whole-graph phonetic loan.
evidence.title: 和 - Wiktionary

evidence.text: The 禾 entry identifies Mandarin hé, Middle Chinese hwa, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[ɢ]ˤoj, glossed as growing grain. This gives the component’s pronunciation and sense independently of 和; it does not establish a sound-based borrowing from a named depicted object.
evidence.title: 禾 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

evidence.field: pronunciation and phonetic series of 和
evidence.text: For 和, this page gives Mandarin hé, Cantonese wo4, and a Zhengzhang phonetic-series table where 禾 and 和 share Old Chinese *ɡoːl for the level-tone reading; it also lists *ɡoːls for a departing-tone reading. It lists 咊 and 龢 as alternative forms but does not establish a direct linear ancestry among them.
evidence.title: 和 - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry organizes readings separately: hè includes sound response, answering or responding, and poetic matching; hé includes fit or appropriateness, harmony, peace, mildness, warmth, conjunction, and sum. It cites classical and later texts, including Analects, Xunzi, Zuozhuan, and later works. These citations show distinct uses but are not a dated chronology of semantic change.

gaps: The earliest attested graphic forms and relative chronology of 龢 and 和 remain unsettled by the pages inspected here. Wiktionary displays historical-form categories without readable glyphs, while the searched secondary account could not be opened for inspection.

The MOE dictionary verifies a Shuowen analysis of 和 as 口 semantic and 禾 phonetic. The separate Shuowen entry for 龢 as 从龠禾聲 is documented in the dossier, but was not independently reopened in this invocation.
The function of 口 is consistent with the MOE account and Shuowen gloss 相應, but whether its motivation is mouth/speech, singing, or an earlier account involving taste is unresolved here.

Citation examples demonstrate response, social harmony, peace and other uses, but the first dated attestation of each sense and a chronological semantic chain were not established. Do not infer semantic chronology from the MOE dictionary’s sense order.

The proposed phonetic component 禾 is a component within a phono-semantic graph. No independent whole-graph loan claim is established, and the original referent/name of 禾 is not needed to support its later phonetic role.

Modern readings checked here include Mandarin hé for 禾 and 和 and Cantonese wo4 for both in Wiktionary; historical comparison is limited to the explicitly named Zhengzhang and Baxter–Sagart systems. The wider dossier’s readings in Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese were not reverified.

No historical glyph image was selected. Searches returned general samples or unrelated character files, not an identified 和/龢 glyph with verified reuse provenance. The Xiaoxuetang query did not expose a specific form record in the opened page.

limitations.text: Search results exposed Commons file pages for general oracle-bone and bronze examples, but inspected descriptions did not identify a 和 or 龢 glyph. The Xiaoxuetang official query page opened, but the inspected text exposed no specific 和 candidate or image URL. No candidate met the identity and provenance requirements for selection.
